title.zh: 卷79 列傳第44 外戚
title.raw: 卷79 列傳第44 外戚 Volume 79 Biographies 44: Imperial Affines

sentences.zh: 隋書卷七十九列傳第四十四

translations.literal: Book of Sui, Volume 79, Biographies 44
translations.idiomatic: Book of Sui, Volume 79, Biographies 44

sentences.zh: ○外戚

translations.literal: ○ Imperial Affines
translations.idiomatic: ○ Imperial Affines

sentences.zh: 曆觀前代外戚之家，乘母后之權以取高位厚秩者多矣，然而鮮有克終之美，必罹顛覆之患，何哉？

translations.literal: Looking through successive ages at households of imperial affines, there were many who, relying on the empress's authority, seized high rank and generous emoluments; yet few ever achieved a fine end—they invariably met with the calamity of overturn. Why was this?
translations.idiomatic: Surveying the imperial affines of earlier dynasties, one finds countless families who rode an empress's power to high office and rich stipends, yet scarcely any who finished well; ruin was almost inevitable. Why?

sentences.zh: 皆由乎無德而尊，不知紀極，忽于滿盈之戒，罔念高危之咎，故鬼瞰其室，憂必及之。

translations.literal: All were because, honored without virtue, they did not know moderation; heedless of the warning against fullness to overflowing, unmindful of the fault of standing in extreme peril—therefore spirits peered into their chambers, and affliction was bound to reach them.
translations.idiomatic: The reason lay in gaining rank without merit, in losing all sense of limit, in ignoring the lesson that plenty invites spillover and high position invites fall—the house watched by ghosts, and trouble never far behind.

sentences.zh: 夫其誠著艱難，功宣社稷，不以謙沖自牧，未免顛蹶之禍，而況道不足以濟時，仁不足以利物，自矜於己，以富貴驕人者乎？

translations.literal: Even those whose sincerity shone through hardship and whose achievements proclaimed the altars of state, if they did not govern themselves with humility and restraint, could not escape the calamity of a fall—how much more those whose Way was insufficient to rescue the age, whose benevolence was insufficient to benefit things, who prided themselves and flaunted wealth and rank before others?
translations.idiomatic: Even men whose loyalty had been proved in hardship and whose service had strengthened the realm, if they failed to keep themselves humble, still risked ruin—what then of those whose conduct could not steady the times, whose kindness could not help others, who merely preened on their own good fortune and lorded their riches over everyone else?

sentences.zh: 此呂、霍、上官、閻、梁、竇、鄧所以繼踵而亡滅者也。

translations.literal: This is why the houses of Lü, Huo, Shangguan, Yan, Liang, Dou, and Deng followed one another in succession yet perished.
translations.idiomatic: This is why the Lü, Huo, Shangguan, Yan, Liang, Dou, and Deng clans rose in turn only to be destroyed.

sentences.zh: 昔文皇潛躍之際，獻後便相推轂，煬帝大橫方兆，蕭妃密勿經綸，是以恩禮綢繆，始終不易。

translations.literal: Formerly, when Emperor Wen was still rising in obscurity, Empress Xian already helped turn the wheel of state; when Emperor Yang's great mandate was just appearing, Consort Xiao took part in secret counsel on affairs of state—thus favor and ceremony were intimate and unchanging from first to last.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen was still struggling toward power, Empress Xian already shared in steering the realm; when Emperor Yang's reign was taking shape, Lady Xiao joined him in the closest counsel. Favor and ceremony therefore ran deep and held steady to the end.

sentences.zh: 然內外親戚，莫預朝權，昆弟在位，亦無殊寵。

translations.literal: Yet among kinsmen within and without, none shared in court power; brothers who held office likewise received no extraordinary favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet none of their kin, whether by blood or marriage, was allowed into real power at court, and even brothers who held office received no special indulgence.

sentences.zh: 至於居擅玉堂，家稱金穴，暉光戚裡，重灼四方，將三司以比儀，命五侯而同拜者，終始一代，寂無聞焉。

translations.literal: As for those who monopolized the jade hall, whose households were called gold caves, whose brilliance lit the imperial affines and whose weight scorched the four quarters, who were paired in ceremony with the Three Excellencies and ordered the Five Marquises to bow with them—throughout a whole generation, not a whisper was heard of such things.
translations.idiomatic: As for the sort who seize the halls of state, whose homes are proverbial treasure vaults, whose glare dazzles the whole imperial clan and burns across the empire, who are treated like the Three Excellencies and have the Five Marquises bow beside them—for an entire reign there was not a trace of that.

sentences.zh: 考之前王，可謂矯其弊矣。

translations.literal: Considering the former kings, one may say they corrected this abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Measured against earlier rulers, the Sui emperors may be said to have corrected that abuse.

sentences.zh: 故雖時經擾攘，無有陷於不義，市朝遷貿，而皆得以保全。

translations.literal: Therefore, although the age passed through turmoil, none fell into injustice; though markets and courts shifted and changed, all were able to preserve themselves.
translations.idiomatic: So even when the times turned violent, none of these affines was driven into disgrace; though power shifted in the capital, they were still able to come through intact.

sentences.zh: 比夫憑藉寵私，階緣恩澤，乘其非據，旋就顛隕者，豈可同日而言哉！

translations.literal: Compared with those who relied on private favor, climbed by grace and bounty, seized what was not theirs to hold, and swiftly met with ruin—how can they be spoken of on the same day!
translations.idiomatic: How can that be mentioned in the same breath as those who traded on private favor, climbed by imperial indulgence, seized what they had no right to hold, and were overturned almost at once?

sentences.zh: 此所謂愛之以禮，能改覆車。

translations.literal: This is what is called loving them by means of ritual, and being able to overturn the overturned cart.
translations.idiomatic: This is what it means to love one's kin with proper restraint and to keep the overturned cart from rolling again.

sentences.zh: 輒敘其事，為《外戚傳》雲。

translations.literal: I therefore set forth these affairs and make them the "Biographies of Imperial Affines."
translations.idiomatic: I therefore relate these matters in the Biographies of Imperial Affines.

sentences.zh: ○高祖外家呂氏

translations.literal: ○ The Lü Clan, Maternal Kin of Gaozu
translations.idiomatic: ○ The Lü Clan, Maternal Kin of Gaozu

sentences.zh: 高祖外家呂氏，其族蓋微，平齊之後，求訪不知所在。

translations.literal: Gaozu's maternal kin, the Lü clan, were in origin a humble family; after the pacification of Qi, searches were made but their whereabouts were unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's mother's people, the Lü, were of humble origin; after the conquest of Qi, officials searched for them but could not find where they were.

sentences.zh: 至開皇初，濟南郡上言，有男子呂永吉，自稱有姑字苦桃，為楊忠妻。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, Jinan commandery reported that a man named Lü Yongji claimed to have an aunt styled Kutao who had been the wife of Yang Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaihuang era, Jinan commandery reported that a man named Lü Yongji claimed an aunt called Kutao had been the wife of Yang Zhong.

sentences.zh: 勘驗知是舅子，始追贈外祖雙周為上柱國、太尉、八州諸軍事、青州刺史，封齊郡公，諡曰敬，外祖母姚氏為齊敬公夫人。

translations.literal: On investigation it was known that he was a nephew by the maternal line; only then were posthumous honors conferred on the maternal grandfather Shuangzhou as Supreme Pillar of State, Grand Commandant, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Eight Prefectures, and Governor of Qing Province, enfeoffed as Duke of Qi commandery with the posthumous title Jing; the maternal grandmother, the Yao clan, was made Lady of Duke Jing of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation showed he was indeed a nephew on the mother's side. The court then posthumously honored the maternal grandfather Shuangzhou as Supreme Pillar of State, Grand Commandant, commander of military affairs in eight prefectures, and governor of Qing, enfeoffing him as Duke of Qi with the posthumous name Jing; the maternal grandmother, née Yao, was titled Lady of Duke Jing of Qi.

sentences.zh: 詔並改葬，于齊州立廟，置守塚十家。

translations.literal: An edict ordered them all reburied, a temple established in Qi province, and ten households appointed to guard the tombs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered new burials, a temple built in Qi province, and ten households assigned to tend the graves.

sentences.zh: 以永吉襲爵，留在京師。

translations.literal: Yongji was made to inherit the title and was kept in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yongji inherited the title and remained in the capital.

sentences.zh: 大業中，授上党郡太守，性識庸劣，職務不理。

translations.literal: During the Daye era he was appointed Governor of Shangdang commandery; his nature and understanding were coarse and inferior, and he did not attend to his duties.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daye period he was made governor of Shangdang, but his mind was dull and he neglected his office.

sentences.zh: 後去官，不知所終。

translations.literal: Later he left office; no one knows how he ended.
translations.idiomatic: He later left office, and nothing more is known of him.

sentences.zh: 永吉從父道貴，性尤頑騃，言詞鄙陋。

translations.literal: Yongji's father's younger cousin Daogui was by nature especially stubborn and dull, and his speech was vulgar and crude.
translations.idiomatic: Yongji's cousin Daogui was even more obstinate and slow-witted, and his speech was coarse.

sentences.zh: 初自鄉里征入長安，上見之悲泣。

translations.literal: When he was first summoned from the countryside into Chang'an, the emperor, on seeing him, wept in grief.
translations.idiomatic: When he was first summoned from the countryside to Chang'an, the emperor wept at the sight of him.

sentences.zh: 道貴略無戚容，但連呼高祖名，雲：「種末定不可偷，大似苦桃姊。」

translations.literal: Daogui showed scarcely any look of kinship feeling; he only kept calling Gaozu by his personal name, saying, "The seed is not yet fixed and must not be stolen—it is very like Elder Sister Kutao."
translations.idiomatic: Daogui showed no sign of family feeling at all. He only kept shouting Gaozu's personal name, saying, "The seed isn't set yet—you can't steal it. You're just like Big Sister Kutao."

sentences.zh: 是後數犯忌諱，動致違忤，上甚耽之。

translations.literal: Thereafter he repeatedly violated taboos and constantly gave offense; the emperor was deeply troubled by him.
translations.idiomatic: After that he broke taboo after taboo and constantly gave offense, until the emperor could hardly bear him.

sentences.zh: 乃命高熲厚加供給，不許接對朝士。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered Gao Jiong to supply him generously and forbade him to meet and converse with court officials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Gao Jiong to provide for him generously but forbade him to associate with court officials.

sentences.zh: 拜上儀同三司，出為濟南太守，令即之任，斷其入朝。

translations.literal: He was appointed Senior Master of Uniformity of the Third Rank and sent out as Governor of Jinan, ordered to take up his post at once and cut off from attending court.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Senior Master of Uniformity of the Third Rank and sent out as governor of Jinan with orders to take up his post at once and never return to court.

sentences.zh: 道貴還至本郡，高自崇重，每與人言，自稱皇舅。

translations.literal: When Daogui returned to his home commandery, he held himself in high esteem; whenever he spoke with others he called himself the emperor's maternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Back in his home commandery, Daogui put on great airs and told everyone he was the emperor's uncle.

sentences.zh: 數將儀衛出入閭裡，從故人游宴，官民鹹苦之。

translations.literal: He often led guards and attendants in and out of the lanes, followed old acquaintances to feasts and revels, and officials and commoners alike suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: He often paraded through the streets with an escort, carousing with old friends, to the misery of officials and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 後郡廢，終於家，子孫無聞焉。

translations.literal: Later the commandery was abolished; he died at home, and nothing was heard of his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: When the commandery was later abolished, he died at home. Nothing more is known of his descendants.

sentences.zh: 獨孤羅弟陀

translations.literal: Dugu Luo and his brother Tuo
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Luo and His Brother Tuo

sentences.zh: 獨孤羅，字羅仁，雲中人也。

translations.literal: Dugu Luo, styled Luoren, was a native of Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Luo, styled Luoren, was a native of Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 父信，初仕魏為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Xin at first served Wei as Governor of Jing province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xin first served Northern Wei as governor of Jing province.

sentences.zh: 武帝之入關也，信棄父母妻子西歸長安，曆職顯貴，羅由是遂為高氏所囚。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu entered the passes, Xin abandoned his parents, wife, and children and returned west to Chang'an, passing through offices of eminent rank; because of this Luo was thereupon taken prisoner by the Gao clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu entered the passes, Xin left his parents, wife, and children behind and went west to Chang'an, rising to high office; Luo was left behind and taken prisoner by the Gao clan.

sentences.zh: 信後仕周為大司馬。

translations.literal: Xin later served Zhou as Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Xin later served Zhou as Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 及信為宇文護所誅，羅始見釋，寓居中山，孤貧無以自給。

translations.literal: When Xin was executed by Yuwen Hu, Luo was only then released; he lodged in Zhongshan, alone and poor, with no means to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: After Xin was executed by Yuwen Hu, Luo was at last freed. He lived in Zhongshan, alone and destitute, with no way to support himself.

sentences.zh: 齊將獨孤永業以宗族之故，見而哀之，為買田宅，遺以資畜。

translations.literal: The Qi general Dugu Yongye, because of clan ties, saw him and pitied him, bought him fields and a house, and gave him livestock and goods.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi general Dugu Yongye, a kinsman, took pity on him, bought him land and a house, and gave him livestock and supplies.

sentences.zh: 初，信入關之後，複娶二妻，郭氏生子六人，善、穆、藏、順、陀、整，崔氏生獻皇后。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Xin entered the passes, he took two wives again; the Guo clan bore six sons—Shan, Mu, Zang, Shun, Tuo, and Zheng—and the Cui clan bore Empress Xian.
translations.idiomatic: After Xin entered the passes he had taken two more wives. Lady Guo bore six sons—Shan, Mu, Zang, Shun, Tuo, and Zheng—and Lady Cui bore Empress Xian.

sentences.zh: 及齊亡，高祖為定州總管，獻皇后遣人尋羅，得之，相見悲不自勝，侍御者皆泣。

translations.literal: When Qi perished, Gaozu was Governor-General of Ding province; Empress Xian sent men to search for Luo, found him, and on meeting grieved beyond control—all who attended them wept.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell, Gaozu was governor-general of Dingzhou and Empress Xian sent men to find Luo. When they met, grief overwhelmed them and everyone present wept.

sentences.zh: 於是厚遺車馬財物。

translations.literal: Thereupon she sent him a generous gift of carriages, horses, and valuables.
translations.idiomatic: She then sent him a generous gift of carriages, horses, and valuables.

sentences.zh: 未幾，周武帝以羅功臣子，久淪異域，征拜楚安郡太守。

translations.literal: Before long, Emperor Wu of Zhou, because Luo was the son of a meritorious minister long lost in a foreign land, summoned and appointed him Governor of Chu'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Emperor Wu of Zhou, seeing that Luo was the son of a meritorious minister long stranded in enemy territory, summoned him and made him governor of Chu'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 以疾去官，歸於京師。

translations.literal: Because of illness he left office and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Illness forced him to leave office, and he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 諸弟見羅少長貧賤，每輕侮之，不以兄禮事也。

translations.literal: His younger brothers, seeing that Luo had from youth grown up in poverty and low station, constantly treated him lightly and did not serve him with the rites due an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers, knowing he had grown up poor and far away, often slighted him and did not treat him as an elder brother.

sentences.zh: 然性長者，亦不與諸弟校競長短，後由是重之。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was a man of forbearance and did not contend with his brothers over who was greater or lesser; afterward for this reason they came to respect him.
translations.idiomatic: But Luo was by nature forbearing and never quarreled with them over precedence, and in time they came to respect him for it.

sentences.zh: 及高祖為丞相，拜儀同，常置左右。

translations.literal: When Gaozu became Chancellor, Luo was appointed Master of Uniformity and constantly kept at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu became chancellor, Luo was made Master of Uniformity and kept constantly at his side.

sentences.zh: 既受禪，下詔追贈羅父信官爵曰：「褒德累行，往代通規，追遠慎終，前王盛典。

translations.literal: After he received the abdication, an edict was issued to posthumously confer offices and titles on Luo's father Xin, saying, "To honor virtue and accumulate conduct is the common rule of former ages; to pursue the distant and be careful at the end is the great ceremony of former kings.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu took the throne, he issued an edict posthumously honoring Luo's father Xin: "To reward accumulated virtue is the constant practice of antiquity; to honor the dead and finish well is the great rite of the ancient kings.

sentences.zh: 故柱國信，風宇高曠，獨秀生民，睿哲居宗，清猷映世。

translations.literal: The former Pillar of State Xin bore a lofty and spacious air, standing alone in excellence among the people; wise and perspicacious, he held the ancestral charge; his pure designs shone upon the age.
translations.idiomatic: The late Pillar of State Xin bore himself with lofty breadth, outstanding among men; wise and far-seeing, he upheld the ancestral charge, and his pure designs illuminated the age.

sentences.zh: 宏謀長策，道著於弼諧，緯義經仁，事深於拯濟。

translations.literal: His great plans and long policies made the Way manifest in assisting harmony; weaving righteousness and threading benevolence, his affairs went deep into rescue and relief.
translations.idiomatic: His grand designs made the Way visible in counsel to the throne; in binding righteousness and ordering benevolence, his work went deep into the saving of the realm.

sentences.zh: 方當宣風廊廟，亮采臺階，而運屬艱危，功高弗賞，眷言令範，事切於心。

translations.literal: Just as he was about to spread virtue in the court hall and display his brilliance on the terrace steps, fate met with hardship and peril; his merit was high yet went unrewarded—recalling his fine example, the matter cuts to the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was to bring his influence to the court and lend his light to the throne, fate turned harsh; his merit went unrewarded, and the memory of his example still pierces the heart.

sentences.zh: 今景運初開，椒闈肅建，載懷塗山之義，無忘褒、紀之典。

translations.literal: Now as the bright fortune first opens and the pepper chambers are solemnly established, bearing in mind the righteousness of Tushan, let us not forget the ceremonies of Bao and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Now, as a new reign begins and the inner palace is duly established, mindful of the duty owed at Tushan, let us not forget the precedent set for the houses of Bao and Ji.

sentences.zh: 可贈太師、上柱國、冀定等十州刺史、趙國公，邑萬戶。」

translations.literal: He may be posthumously conferred as Grand Preceptor, Supreme Pillar of State, Governor of ten prefectures including Ji and Ding, and Duke of Zhao state, with a fief of ten thousand households."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor, Supreme Pillar of State, governor of ten prefectures including Ji and Ding, and Duke of Zhao, with a fief of ten thousand households."

sentences.zh: 其諸弟以羅母沒齊，先無夫人之號，不當承襲。

translations.literal: His younger brothers, because Luo's mother had died in Qi and had never borne the title of Lady, held that he ought not to inherit.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers argued that because Luo's mother had died in Qi without ever receiving the title of Lady, he ought not to inherit the dukedom.

sentences.zh: 上以問後，後曰：「羅誠嫡長，不可誣也。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked the empress; the empress said, "Luo is truly the eldest son of the primary wife—this cannot be denied."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked the empress, who replied, "Luo is truly the eldest son of the primary line. That cannot be denied."

sentences.zh: 於是襲爵趙國公。

translations.literal: Thereupon he inherited the title of Duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Luo therefore inherited the title of Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 以其弟善為河內郡公，穆為金泉縣公，藏為武平縣公，陀為武喜縣公，整為千牛備身。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shan was made Duke of Henei commandery, Mu Duke of Jinquan county, Zang Duke of Wuping county, Tuo Duke of Wuxi county, and Zheng an attendant of the Thousand-Ox Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Shan was made Duke of Henei, Mu Duke of Jinquan county, Zang Duke of Wuping county, Tuo Duke of Wuxi county, and Zheng an attendant of the Thousand-Ox Guard.

sentences.zh: 擢拜羅為左領左右將軍，尋遷左衛將軍，前後賞賜不可勝計。

translations.literal: Luo was promoted and appointed General of the Left Retinue of the Left and Right, and soon transferred to General of the Left Guard; rewards before and after were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Luo was promoted to general of the Left Retinue, then transferred to general of the Left Guard, and received rewards beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 久而出為涼州總管，進位上柱國。

translations.literal: After a long while he went out as Governor-General of Liang province and advanced to Supreme Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was sent out as governor-general of Liangzhou and promoted to Supreme Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，征拜左武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: During Renshou he was summoned and appointed Grand General of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou period he was recalled and made grand general of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，改封蜀國公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Luo's fief was changed to Duke of Shu state.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Luo's title was changed to Duke of Shu.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒官，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: Before long he died in office; his posthumous title was Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office not long afterward and was given the posthumous name Gong.

sentences.zh: 子纂嗣，仕至河陽郡尉。

translations.literal: His son Zuan succeeded him and served as Commandant of Heyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zuan inherited the title and rose to commandant of Heyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 纂弟武都，大業末，亦為河陽郡尉。

translations.literal: Zuan's younger brother Wudu, at the end of the Daye era, also became Commandant of Heyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's younger brother Wudu also became commandant of Heyang at the end of the Daye period.

sentences.zh: 庶長子開遠，宇文化及之弑逆也，裴虔通率賊入成象殿，宿衛兵士皆從逆，開遠時為千牛，與獨孤盛力戰於閤下，為賊所執，賊義而舍之。

translations.literal: The eldest son by a concubine, Kaiyuan—when Yuwen Huaji committed regicide, Pei Qiantong led the rebels into Chengxian Hall; the palace guards all followed the rebels. Kaiyuan was then in the Thousand-Ox Guard; together with Dugu Sheng he fought fiercely below the gate-tower, was seized by the rebels, and because of their sense of righteousness they released him.
translations.idiomatic: An elder son by a concubine, Kaiyuan, was serving in the Thousand-Ox Guard when Yuwen Huaji murdered the emperor. Pei Qiantong led the rebels into Chengxian Hall, and the palace guards joined them. Kaiyuan and Dugu Sheng fought fiercely below the gate-tower, were captured, and then released because the rebels admired their courage.

sentences.zh: 善後官至柱國。

translations.literal: Shan later reached the office of Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: Shan later rose to Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 卒，子覽嗣，仕至左候衛將軍，大業末卒。

translations.literal: When he died, his son Lan succeeded him, served as General of the Left Garrison Guard, and died at the end of the Daye era.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his son Lan inherited the line, rose to general of the Left Garrison Guard, and died at the end of the Daye period.

sentences.zh: 獨孤陀，字黎邪。

translations.literal: Dugu Tuo, styled Lixie.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Tuo, styled Lixie.

sentences.zh: 仕周胥附上士，坐父徙蜀郡十餘年。

translations.literal: He served Zhou as a gentleman-attendant of Xufu; because of his father's case he was banished to Shu commandery for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: He served Zhou as a gentleman-attendant of Xufu and, because of his father's case, was exiled to Shu commandery for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 宇文護被誅，始歸長安。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Hu was executed, he at last returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuwen Hu was executed, he was at last allowed to return to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，拜上開府、右領左右將軍。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, Tuo was appointed Senior Opener of the Mansion and General of the Right Retinue of the Left and Right.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Tuo was made Senior Opener of the Mansion and general of the Right Retinue.

sentences.zh: 久之，出為郢州刺史，進位上大將軍，累轉延州刺史。

translations.literal: After a long while he went out as Governor of E prefecture, advanced to Grand General, and was transferred in succession to Governor of Yan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was sent out as governor of E prefecture, promoted to grand general, and later transferred to governor of Yan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 好左道。

translations.literal: He was fond of heterodox ways.
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted to heterodox cult practices.

sentences.zh: 其妻母先事貓鬼，因轉入其家。

translations.literal: His wife's mother had first served the cat-demon, and the practice thereby passed into his household.
translations.idiomatic: His wife's mother had first worshipped the cat-demon, and the practice passed into his household.

sentences.zh: 上微聞而不之信也。

translations.literal: The emperor heard a little of it but did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard rumors but did not believe them.

sentences.zh: 會獻皇后及楊素妻鄭氏俱有疾，召醫者視之，皆曰：「此貓鬼疾也。」

translations.literal: It happened that both Empress Xian and Yang Su's wife, the Zheng clan, fell ill; physicians were summoned to examine them, and all said, "This is cat-demon sickness."
translations.idiomatic: Then both Empress Xian and Yang Su's wife, Lady Zheng, fell ill. The physicians they summoned all said, "This is cat-demon sickness."

sentences.zh: 上以陀後之異母弟，陀妻楊素之異母妹，由是意陀所為，陰令其兄穆以情喻之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Tuo was the empress's younger half-brother and Tuo's wife was Yang Su's younger half-sister, therefore suspected Tuo's doing and secretly ordered his elder brother Mu to explain the situation to him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Tuo was the empress's younger half-brother and his wife was Yang Su's younger half-sister, the emperor suspected Tuo and secretly had his brother Mu reason with him.

sentences.zh: 上又避左右諷陀，陀言無有。

translations.literal: The emperor also, avoiding attendants, admonished Tuo indirectly; Tuo said there was nothing of the kind.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also spoke to him privately, hinting at the matter, but Tuo denied everything.

sentences.zh: 上不悅，左轉遷州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and transferred him to the left as Governor of Qian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Displeased, the emperor demoted him to governor of Qian prefecture.

sentences.zh: 出怨言。

translations.literal: He uttered words of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He began to complain openly.

sentences.zh: 上令左僕射高熲、納言蘇威、大理正皇甫孝緒、大理丞楊遠等雜治之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the Left Vice Director Gao Jiong, the Palace Counselor Su Wei, the Chief of the Court of Judicial Review Huangfu Xiaoxu, the Assistant of the Court of Judicial Review Yang Yuan, and others jointly to try the case.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Left Vice Director Gao Jiong, Palace Counselor Su Wei, Chief of the Court of Judicial Review Huangfu Xiaoxu, Assistant of the Court of Judicial Review Yang Yuan, and others to investigate jointly.

sentences.zh: 陀婢徐阿尼言，本從陀母家來，常事貓鬼。

translations.literal: Tuo's maid Xu Ani testified that she had originally come from Tuo's mother's household and had constantly served the cat-demon.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo's maid Xu Ani testified that she had come from his mother's household and had long served the cat-demon.

sentences.zh: 每以子日夜祀之。

translations.literal: Every night at the hour of zi she sacrificed to it.
translations.idiomatic: Every night at the hour of zi she made offerings to it.

sentences.zh: 言子者鼠也。

translations.literal: "Zi" means the rat.
translations.idiomatic: By "zi" she meant the rat—the hour of the rat.

sentences.zh: 其貓鬼每殺人者，所死家財物潛移於畜貓鬼家。

translations.literal: Whenever the cat-demon killed someone, the property of the dead household was secretly transferred to the household that kept the cat-demon.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the cat-demon killed someone, the victim's wealth was secretly transferred to the household that kept the demon.

sentences.zh: 陀嘗從家中素酒，其妻曰：「無錢可酤。」

translations.literal: Tuo once asked for wine at home; his wife said, "There is no money to buy any."
translations.idiomatic: Tuo once asked for wine at home. His wife said, "We have no money to buy any."

sentences.zh: 陀因謂阿尼曰：「可令貓鬼向越公家，使我足錢也。」

translations.literal: Tuo thereupon said to Ani, "You can have the cat-demon go to Duke Yue's household and get me enough money."
translations.idiomatic: Tuo then told Ani, "Send the cat-demon to Duke Yue's house and get me enough money."

sentences.zh: 阿尼便咒之歸。

translations.literal: Ani then chanted to send it back.
translations.idiomatic: Ani chanted the spell to send it off.

sentences.zh: 數日，貓鬼向素家。

translations.literal: Within several days the cat-demon went toward Yang Su's household.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days the cat-demon was sent to Yang Su's house.

sentences.zh: 十一年，上初從并州還，陀於園中謂阿尼曰：「可令貓鬼向皇后所，使多賜吾物。」

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, when the emperor had just returned from Bing province, Tuo said to Ani in the garden, "You can have the cat-demon go to the empress's quarters and make her bestow many things on me."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, soon after the emperor returned from Bingzhou, Tuo told Ani in the garden, "Send the cat-demon to the empress and make her give me more gifts."

sentences.zh: 阿尼複咒之，遂入宮中。

translations.literal: Ani again chanted, and it thereupon entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Ani chanted again, and the demon entered the palace.

sentences.zh: 楊遠乃于門下外省遣阿尼呼貓鬼。

translations.literal: Yang Yuan then, at the Outer Office of the Gate Department, sent Ani to summon the cat-demon.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuan then had Ani summon the cat-demon at the Outer Office of the Gate Department.

sentences.zh: 阿尼於是夜中置香粥一盆，以匙扣而呼之曰：「貓女可來，無住宮中。」

translations.literal: Ani then, in the middle of the night, set out a basin of fragrant porridge, knocked it with a spoon, and called, "Cat-girl, you may come—do not stay in the palace."
translations.idiomatic: That night Ani set out a bowl of fragrant porridge, tapped it with a spoon, and called, "Cat-girl, come—but do not stay in the palace."

sentences.zh: 久之，阿尼色正青，若被牽曳者，雲貓鬼已至。

translations.literal: After a long while Ani's face turned pure blue, as if she were being dragged, and she said the cat-demon had arrived.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while her face turned blue, as if she were being pulled, and she said the cat-demon had come.

sentences.zh: 上以其事下公卿，奇章公牛弘曰：「妖由人興，殺其人可以絕矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor submitted the matter to the dukes and ministers; Niuzhang Duke Niu Hong said, "Omens arise through men—kill the man and it can be ended."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor referred the case to the high officials. Niu Hong, Duke of Qizhang, said, "Such evil rises through men. Kill the man and it will end."

sentences.zh: 上令以犢車載陀夫妻，將賜死於其家。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Tuo and his wife loaded into a calf cart and sent to be granted death at their home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Tuo and his wife taken in a cart to their home to be put to death.

sentences.zh: 陀弟司勳侍中整詣闕求哀，於是免陀死，除名為民，以其妻楊氏為尼。

translations.literal: Tuo's younger brother Zheng, Director of the Department of Merit and Attendant-in-Ordinary, went to the palace gate to plead for mercy; thereupon Tuo was spared death, struck from the registers and made a commoner, and his wife, the Yang clan, was made a nun.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo's brother Zheng, Director of the Department of Merit and attendant-in-ordinary, pleaded at court for mercy. Tuo was spared death, reduced to commoner status, and his wife, Lady Yang, was made a nun.

sentences.zh: 先是，有人訟其母為人貓鬼所殺者，上以為妖妄，怒而遣之。

translations.literal: Earlier, someone had sued, claiming his mother had been killed by another's cat-demon; the emperor regarded it as demonic delusion, grew angry, and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, a man had sued, claiming his mother had been killed by another person's cat-demon. The emperor dismissed it as superstitious nonsense and sent him away in anger.

sentences.zh: 及此，詔誅被訟行貓鬼家。

translations.literal: At this point an edict ordered the execution of the household accused of practicing the cat-demon.
translations.idiomatic: Now an edict ordered the household accused in that earlier suit to be executed.

sentences.zh: 經未幾而卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died not long afterward.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，追念舅氏，聽以禮葬，乃下詔曰：「外氏衰禍，獨孤陀不幸早世，遷卜有期。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang took the throne, recalling his maternal kin, he permitted burial according to ritual and issued an edict saying, "My mother's clan has suffered decline and calamity; Dugu Tuo, unhappily, died young, and the time for moving the tomb and setting the burial date has come.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, mindful of his mother's kin, he allowed Tuo a proper burial and issued an edict: "My mother's clan has fallen on hard times. Dugu Tuo died young, and the time has come to move his tomb and set his burial.

sentences.zh: 言念渭陽之情，追懷傷切，宜加禮命，允備哀榮。

translations.literal: Speaking of the feeling of Weiyang, the pursuit of remembrance is grievously cutting; ritual honors should be increased, and mourning glory fully granted.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful of the bond between maternal kin, and deeply grieved in remembrance, let ritual honors be added and full mourning glory granted.

sentences.zh: 可贈正議大夫。」

translations.literal: He may be posthumously conferred as Grand Master of Correct Discussion."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously honored as Grand Master of Correct Discussion."

sentences.zh: 帝意猶不已，複下詔曰：「舅氏之尊，戚屬斯重，而降年弗永，凋落相繼。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was still not satisfied, and he again issued an edict saying, "The honor due maternal uncles, the weight of affinal kin—yet their allotted years are not long, and they fall away one after another.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was still not satisfied and issued another edict: "Maternal uncles are men of great honor, and affinal kin carry heavy weight—yet their years are short, and they fall away one after another.

sentences.zh: 緬惟先往，宜崇徽秩。

translations.literal: Looking back on those who went before, their eminent ranks should be exalted.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking of those who have gone before, their ranks should be raised in honor.

sentences.zh: 複贈銀青光祿大夫。」

translations.literal: He was again posthumously conferred as Grand Master of the Silver-Green Light."
translations.idiomatic: He was again posthumously honored as Grand Master of the Silver-Green Light."

sentences.zh: 有二子：延福、延壽。

translations.literal: He had two sons: Yanfu and Yanshou.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Yanfu and Yanshou.

sentences.zh: 陀弟整，官至幽州刺史，大業初卒，贈金紫光祿大夫，平鄉侯。

translations.literal: Tuo's younger brother Zheng reached the office of Governor of You province; he died at the beginning of the Daye era and was posthumously conferred as Grand Master of the Gold-Purple Light and Marquis of Pingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo's brother Zheng rose to governor of You province, died early in the Daye period, and was posthumously honored as Grand Master of the Gold-Purple Light and Marquis of Pingxiang.

sentences.zh: 蕭巋子琮琮弟瓛

translations.literal: Xiao Kui; his son Cong; Cong's younger brother Huan
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Kui; His Son Cong; Cong's Brother Huan

sentences.zh: 蕭巋，字仁遠，梁昭明太子統之孫也。

translations.literal: Xiao Kui, styled Renyuan, was a grandson of Liang's Crown Prince Zhaoming, Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Kui, styled Renyuan, was a grandson of Liang's Crown Prince Zhaoming, Xiao Tong.

sentences.zh: 父詧，初封岳陽王，鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: His father Cha was at first enfeoffed as Prince of Yueyang and garrisoned Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cha was first enfeoffed as Prince of Yueyang and posted at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，其兄河東王譽與其叔父湘東王繹不協，為繹所害。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion, his elder brother Prince of Hedong, Yu, was at odds with their uncle Prince of Xiangdong, Yi, and was killed by Yi.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion, his elder brother Prince Yu of Hedong fell out with their uncle Prince Yi of Xiangdong and was killed by him.

sentences.zh: 及繹嗣位，詧稱籓於西魏，乞師請討繹。

translations.literal: When Yi succeeded to the throne, Cha declared himself a vassal of Western Wei, begged troops, and requested a campaign against Yi.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi took the throne, Cha submitted to Western Wei as a vassal, asked for troops, and requested a campaign against Yi.

sentences.zh: 周太祖以詧為梁主，遣柱國於謹等率騎五萬襲繹，滅之。

translations.literal: Taizu of Zhou made Cha ruler of Liang and sent the Pillar of State Yu Jin and others at the head of fifty thousand horsemen to strike Yi and destroy him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu of Zhou installed Cha as ruler of Liang and sent the Pillar of State Yu Jin with fifty thousand horsemen to strike Yi and destroy him.

sentences.zh: 詧遂都江陵，有荊郡、其西平州延袤三百里之地，稱皇帝于其國，車服節文一同王者。

translations.literal: Cha then moved the capital to Jiangling, held Jing commandery and Xiping prefecture to the west—a territory three hundred li in extent—and styled himself emperor in his state; carriage regalia, dress, and ritual regulations were all the same as a king's.
translations.idiomatic: Cha then moved his capital to Jiangling, holding Jing commandery and Xiping prefecture to the west—a domain three hundred li across—and proclaimed himself emperor; his carriage regalia, dress, and ritual forms matched those of a true sovereign.

sentences.zh: 仍置江陵總管，以兵戍之。

translations.literal: A Jiangling Governor-General was still established to garrison it with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou still stationed a governor-general at Jiangling with troops to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 詧薨，巋嗣位，年號天保。

translations.literal: When Cha died, Kui succeeded him, with the era name Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: When Cha died, Kui succeeded him under the era name Tianbao.

sentences.zh: 巋俊辯有才學，兼好內典。

translations.literal: Kui was handsome, eloquent, and learned, and was also fond of Buddhist scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: Kui was handsome, eloquent, and learned, and also devoted to Buddhist scriptures.

sentences.zh: 周武帝平齊之後，巋來賀，帝享之甚歡。

translations.literal: After Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi, Kui came to offer congratulations; the emperor entertained him with great delight.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu of Zhou conquered Qi, Kui came to offer congratulations and was entertained with great delight.

sentences.zh: 親彈琵琶，令巋起舞，巋曰：「陛下親禦五糸玄，臣敢不同百獸！」

translations.literal: The emperor personally played the pipa and ordered Kui to dance; Kui said, "Your Majesty personally handles the five-stringed dark lute—how dare your servant not join the hundred beasts!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor played the pipa himself and ordered Kui to dance. Kui replied, "Your Majesty plays the five-stringed lute—how dare I not join the hundred beasts in response!"

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，恩禮彌厚，遣使賜金五百兩，銀千兩，布帛萬匹，馬五百匹。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, favor and ceremony grew still richer; envoys were sent to bestow five hundred taels of gold, a thousand taels of silver, ten thousand bolts of cloth and silk, and five hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, favor and ceremony grew still richer. Envoys were sent with five hundred taels of gold, a thousand taels of silver, ten thousand bolts of cloth and silk, and five hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 巋來朝，上甚敬焉，詔巋位在王公之上。

translations.literal: Kui came to court; the emperor greatly respected him and ordered that Kui's rank stand above the kings and dukes.
translations.idiomatic: When Kui came to court, the emperor treated him with great respect and ordered that his rank stand above the kings and dukes.

sentences.zh: 巋被服端麗，進退閒雅，天子矚目，百僚傾慕。

translations.literal: Kui's dress and adornment were dignified and beautiful; in advancing and withdrawing he was easy and elegant—the Son of Heaven fixed his gaze on him, and the hundred officials looked on him with admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Kui dressed with dignified elegance and moved with easy grace. The emperor watched him closely, and the whole court looked on with admiration.

sentences.zh: 賞賜以億計。

translations.literal: Rewards and gifts were reckoned in the hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards and gifts ran into the hundreds of millions.

sentences.zh: 月餘歸籓，帝親餞于滻水之上。

translations.literal: After more than a month he returned to his fief; the emperor personally saw him off on the banks of the Ba River.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month he returned to his domain, and the emperor personally saw him off on the banks of the Ba River.

sentences.zh: 後備禮納其女為晉王妃，又欲以其子瑒尚蘭陵公主。

translations.literal: Later, with full ceremony, his daughter was taken in marriage as consort to the Prince of Jin, and the emperor also wished to marry his son Yang to Princess Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: Later his daughter was married with full ceremony to the Prince of Jin, and the emperor also wished to marry Kui's son Yang to Princess Lanling.

sentences.zh: 由是漸見親待。

translations.literal: From this he gradually came to be treated with intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he was increasingly treated as family.

sentences.zh: 獻皇后言于上曰：「梁主通家，腹心所寄，何勞猜防也。」

translations.literal: Empress Xian said to the emperor, "The Lord of Liang is family by marriage, one in whom your heart is entrusted—why trouble yourself with suspicion and guard?"
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xian told the emperor, "The Lord of Liang is family by marriage, a man you trust with your heart—why trouble yourself with suspicion?"

sentences.zh: 上然之，於是罷江陵總管，巋專制其國。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed; thereupon the Jiangling Governor-General was abolished, and Kui held sole rule over his state.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, abolished the Jiangling governor-general, and let Kui rule his state on his own.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，巋又來朝，賜縑萬匹，珍玩稱是。

translations.literal: After more than a year Kui came to court again and was given ten thousand bolts of fine silk and treasures and curios in like measure.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Kui came to court again and received ten thousand bolts of fine silk and treasures in like measure.

sentences.zh: 及還，上親執手曰：「梁主久滯荊楚，未復舊都，故鄉之念，良軫懷抱。

translations.literal: When he returned, the emperor personally took his hand and said, "The Lord of Liang has long been detained in Jing-Chu and has not yet recovered his old capital; thoughts of home must weigh heavily on your heart.
translations.idiomatic: When he departed, the emperor took his hand and said, "You have long been held in Jing-Chu and have not yet recovered your old capital. Thoughts of home must weigh heavily on your heart.

sentences.zh: 朕當振旅長江，相送旋反耳。」

translations.literal: I shall raise an army on the Yangzi and send you back in triumph."
translations.idiomatic: I shall raise an army on the Yangzi and send you home in triumph."

sentences.zh: 巋拜謝而去。

translations.literal: Kui bowed in thanks and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Kui bowed in thanks and departed.

sentences.zh: 其年五月，寢疾，臨終上表曰：「臣以庸暗，曲荷天慈，寵冠外籓，恩逾連山，爰及子女，尚主婚王。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of that year he fell ill in bed; on his deathbed he submitted a memorial saying, "Your servant, dim and mediocre, has undeservedly received Heaven's kindness; favor has crowned me above the outer fiefs, grace has surpassed linked mountains; even my sons and daughters have married princesses and princes.
translations.idiomatic: That fifth month he fell ill. On his deathbed he submitted a memorial: "Your servant, dull and unworthy, has undeservedly received Heaven's kindness. Favor has crowned me above the outer fiefs, grace has surpassed the mountains themselves; even my sons and daughters have married into the imperial house.

sentences.zh: 每願躬擐甲胄，身先士卒，掃蕩逋寇，上報明時。

translations.literal: I have always wished to don armor myself, take the lead before the soldiers, sweep away the fleeing bandits, and repay the enlightened age above.
translations.idiomatic: I have always wished to don armor myself, lead the soldiers in person, sweep away the rebels, and repay this enlightened age.

sentences.zh: 而攝生乖舛，遽罹屙疾，屬纊在辰，顧陰待謝。

translations.literal: Yet in nurturing life I went astray and suddenly met with wasting sickness; the silk of death is at hand, and I await the shade in farewell.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I failed in caring for my health and have suddenly fallen gravely ill. Death is near, and I await the end.

sentences.zh: 長違聖世，感戀嗚咽，遺嗣孤藐，特乞降慈。

translations.literal: Long parted from the sage age, I grieve and sob in longing; my orphaned heirs are young and small—I specially beg your lowered kindness.
translations.idiomatic: I must leave this sage age, and grief overwhelms me. My orphaned heirs are young and helpless—I beg your mercy for them.

sentences.zh: 伏願聖躬與山嶽同固，皇基等天日俱永，臣雖九泉，實無遣恨。」

translations.literal: I bow and wish that your sacred person may be as firm as mountains and hills, that the imperial foundation may last as long as heaven and sun together—even in the nine springs, your servant would truly have no regret left behind."
translations.idiomatic: I pray that your sacred person may stand firm as the mountains, that the imperial foundation may last as long as heaven and sun—even in the grave I shall have no regret."

sentences.zh: 並獻所服金裝劍，上覽而嗟悼焉。

translations.literal: He also presented the gold-mounted sword he had worn; the emperor read it and sighed in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He also presented the gold-mounted sword he had worn. The emperor read the memorial and sighed in grief.

sentences.zh: 巋在位二十三年，年四十四薨，梁之臣子諡曰孝明皇帝，廟號世宗。

translations.literal: Kui reigned twenty-three years and died at age forty-four; Liang's ministers and subjects gave him the posthumous title Emperor Xiaoming and the temple name Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: Kui reigned twenty-three years and died at forty-four. Liang's ministers gave him the posthumous title Emperor Xiaoming and the temple name Shizong.

sentences.zh: 子琮嗣。

translations.literal: His son Cong succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 巋著《孝經》、《周易義記》及《大小乘幽微》十四卷，行於世。

translations.literal: Kui authored the Classic of Filial Piety, Records of the Meaning of the Book of Changes, and Subtleties of the Greater and Lesser Vehicles in fourteen scrolls, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Kui wrote the Classic of Filial Piety, Records of the Meaning of the Book of Changes, and Subtleties of the Greater and Lesser Vehicles in fourteen scrolls, all of which circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 琮字溫文，性寬仁，有大度，倜儻不羈，博學有文義。

translations.literal: Cong, styled Wenwen, was by nature generous and humane, possessed of great breadth, free and unrestrained, broadly learned and skilled in literary meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Cong, styled Wenwen, was generous and humane, broad-minded, free-spirited and unrestrained, widely learned and accomplished in letters.

sentences.zh: 兼善弓馬，遣人伏地著帖，琮馳馬射之，十發十中，持帖者亦不懼。

translations.literal: He was also skilled in bow and horse; he had a man lie prone on the ground with a target affixed, and Cong galloped and shot at it—ten shots, ten hits—and the man holding the target was not afraid.
translations.idiomatic: He was also skilled with bow and horse. He had a man lie prone with a target on his back, then galloped and shot at it—ten shots, ten hits—and the man holding the target did not flinch.

sentences.zh: 初封東陽王，尋立為梁太子。

translations.literal: He was at first enfeoffed as Prince of Dongyang and soon established as Liang's crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed as Prince of Dongyang and soon made crown prince of Liang.

sentences.zh: 及嗣位，上賜璽書曰：「負荷堂構，其事甚重，雖窮憂勞，常須自力。

translations.literal: When he succeeded to the throne, the emperor bestowed a sealed letter saying, "To bear the hall and framework is a weighty matter; though exhausted with worry and toil, you must constantly rely on your own strength.
translations.idiomatic: When he succeeded to the throne, the emperor sent a sealed letter: "To bear the weight of the realm is a grave matter. Though worn with worry and toil, you must constantly rely on your own strength.

sentences.zh: 輯諧內外，親任才良，聿遵世業，是所望也。

translations.literal: Harmonize within and without, personally employ the talented and good, and faithfully follow the enterprise of the age—this is what is hoped for.
translations.idiomatic: Harmonize within and without, personally employ the talented and worthy, and faithfully carry on your father's enterprise—that is my hope.

sentences.zh: 彼之疆守，咫尺陳人，水潦之時，特宜警備。

translations.literal: Their frontier garrisons are but a foot away from Chen; in times of flood and rain, special vigilance is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Chen lies just beyond your border. In the rainy season you must be especially vigilant.

sentences.zh: 陳氏比日雖複朝聘相尋，疆埸之間猶未清肅，唯當恃我必不可幹，勿得輕人而不設備。

translations.literal: Though Chen of late has again sent envoys back and forth, the borderlands are still not clear and settled; you should rely on the fact that they cannot possibly resist me, yet must not treat others lightly and fail to make preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Though Chen has lately resumed diplomatic visits, the border is still unsettled. Trust that they cannot possibly defy me—but do not treat them lightly or neglect your defenses.

sentences.zh: 朕與梁國，積世相知，重以親姻，情義彌厚。

translations.literal: I and the state of Liang have known each other through accumulated generations; redoubled by marriage ties, affection and righteousness grow still deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Liang and I have known each other across generations, and marriage ties have made our bond still deeper.

sentences.zh: 江陵之地，朝寄非輕，為國為民，深宜抑割，恆加饘粥，以禮自存。」

translations.literal: The land of Jiangling is no light charge from the court; for state and for people you should deeply restrain yourself, constantly take thin gruel, and preserve yourself through ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Jiangling is no light charge from the court. For the sake of state and people you should restrain yourself, live simply on plain food, and preserve yourself through proper conduct."

sentences.zh: 又賜梁之大臣璽書，誠勉之。

translations.literal: He also bestowed sealed letters on Liang's great ministers, sincerely exhorting them.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent sealed letters to Liang's great ministers, sincerely exhorting them.

sentences.zh: 時琮年號廣運，有識者曰：「運之為字，軍走也，吾君將奔走乎？」

translations.literal: At that time Cong's era name was Guangyun; men of insight said, "The character yun means 'army' and 'flee'—will our lord take to flight?"
translations.idiomatic: Cong's era name was Guangyun. Men of insight said, "The character yun combines 'army' and 'flee'—will our lord take to flight?"

sentences.zh: 其年，琮遣大將軍戚昕以舟師襲陳公安，不克而還。

translations.literal: That year Cong sent the Grand General Qi Xin with a naval force to strike Chen Gong'an but failed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: That year Cong sent Grand General Qi Xin with a naval force to strike Chen's Gong'an but failed and returned.

sentences.zh: 征琮叔父岑入朝，拜為大將軍，封懷義公，因留不遣。

translations.literal: Cong's uncle Cen was summoned to court, appointed Grand General, enfeoffed as Duke of Huaiyi, and thereupon detained and not sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Cong's uncle Cen was summoned to court, made grand general, enfeoffed as Duke of Huaiyi, and detained there.

sentences.zh: 複置江陵總管以監之。

translations.literal: The Jiangling Governor-General was again established to oversee him.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangling governor-general was reinstated to keep watch over him.

sentences.zh: 琮所署大將軍許世武密以城召陳將宜黃侯陳紀，謀泄，琮誅之。

translations.literal: The Grand General Xu Shiwu, whom Cong had appointed, secretly offered the city to summon the Chen general Marquis of Yihuang, Chen Ji; the plot leaked out, and Cong executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Xu Shiwu, whom Cong had appointed, secretly offered the city to Chen general Marquis Chen Ji of Yihuang. When the plot leaked, Cong executed him.

sentences.zh: 後二歲，上征琮入朝，率其臣下二百余人朝于京師，江陵父老莫不隕涕相謂曰：「吾君其不反矣！」

translations.literal: Two years later the emperor summoned Cong to court; he led more than two hundred ministers and subordinates to attend court in the capital, and the elders of Jiangling all shed tears and said to one another, "Our lord will not return!"
translations.idiomatic: Two years later the emperor summoned Cong to court. He led more than two hundred ministers to the capital, and the elders of Jiangling wept and said to one another, "Our lord will not return!"

sentences.zh: 上以琮來朝，遣武鄉公崔弘度將兵戍之。

translations.literal: Because Cong had come to court, the emperor sent Duke of Wuxiang Cui Hongdu to lead troops to garrison the place.
translations.idiomatic: Because Cong had come to court, the emperor sent Duke of Wuxiang Cui Hongdu with troops to garrison Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 軍至鄀州，琮叔父岩及弟瓛等懼弘度掩襲之，遂引陳人至城下，虜居民而叛，於是廢梁國。

translations.literal: When the army reached E prefecture, Cong's uncle Yan and younger brother Huan and others, fearing that Hongdu would launch a surprise attack, thereupon brought Chen men to the foot of the walls, seized the inhabitants, and rebelled—whereupon the state of Liang was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached E prefecture, Cong's uncle Yan and his brother Huan, fearing a surprise attack, brought Chen troops to the walls, seized the inhabitants, and rebelled. The state of Liang was abolished.

sentences.zh: 上遣左僕射高熲安集之，曲赦江陵死罪，給民複十年。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the Left Vice Director Gao Jiong to pacify and settle the region, granted a special pardon for capital crimes in Jiangling, and gave the people tax relief for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Left Vice Director Gao Jiong to pacify the region, granted a special pardon for capital crimes in Jiangling, and gave the people ten years of tax relief.

sentences.zh: 梁二主各給守墓十戶。

translations.literal: To each of the two Liang rulers ten households were assigned to guard the tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Ten households were assigned to guard each of the two Liang rulers' tombs.

sentences.zh: 拜琮為柱國，賜爵莒國公。

translations.literal: Cong was appointed Pillar of State and granted the title Duke of Ju state.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was made Pillar of State and enfeoffed as Duke of Ju.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，以皇后之故，甚見親重。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, because of the empress he was greatly favored and esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Cong was greatly favored because of the empress.

sentences.zh: 拜內史令，改封梁公。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Palace Secretariat and his fief was changed to Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Director of the Palace Secretariat and his title was changed to Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 琮之宗族，緦麻以上，並隨才擢用，於是諸蕭昆弟布列朝廷。

translations.literal: Cong's clansmen, from those in the finest mourning grade upward, were all promoted according to talent; thus the various Xiao brothers were arrayed throughout the court.
translations.idiomatic: Cong's clansmen, even those in the remotest degree of kinship, were promoted according to talent, and Xiao brothers filled the court.

sentences.zh: 琮性淡雅，不以職務自嬰，退朝縱酒而已。

translations.literal: Cong was by nature refined and detached; he did not burden himself with official duties—after court he merely drank freely.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was refined and detached by nature and did not burden himself with office; after court he merely drank.

sentences.zh: 內史令楊約與琮同列，帝令約宣旨誡勵，約複以私情喻之。

translations.literal: The Director of the Palace Secretariat Yang Yue was of the same rank as Cong; the emperor ordered Yue to proclaim the imperial will and admonish him, and Yue again explained it in private terms.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Palace Secretariat Yang Yue, Cong's equal in rank, was ordered to admonish him, and Yue spoke to him privately as well.

sentences.zh: 琮答曰：「琮若複事事，則何異於公哉！」

translations.literal: Cong replied, "If Cong again attended to every matter, how would he differ from you!"
translations.idiomatic: Cong replied, "If I attended to every matter again, how would I differ from you!"

sentences.zh: 約笑而退。

translations.literal: Yue laughed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yue laughed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 約兄素，時為尚書令，見琮嫁從父妹于鉗耳氏，因謂琮曰：「公，帝王之族，望高戚美，何乃適妹鉗耳氏乎？」

translations.literal: Yue's elder brother Su, who was then Director of the Department of State Affairs, saw that Cong had married a younger cousin by the father's line to the Qian'er clan and therefore said to Cong, "Sir, you are of an imperial clan—your standing is high and your affinal beauty great—why marry your sister to the Qian'er clan?"
translations.idiomatic: Yue's brother Su, then Director of the Department of State Affairs, saw that Cong had married a cousin to the Qian'er clan and said, "You are of imperial stock, with high standing and noble connections—why marry your sister to the Qian'er?"

sentences.zh: 琮曰：「前已嫁妹于侯莫陳氏，此複何疑！」

translations.literal: Cong said, "I have already married a sister to the Houmochen clan before—what doubt is there in this!"
translations.idiomatic: Cong said, "I already married one sister to the Houmochen—what is there to question in this!"

sentences.zh: 素曰：「鉗耳，羌也，侯莫陳，虜也，何得相比！」

translations.literal: Su said, "Qian'er are Qiang; Houmochen are barbarians—how can they be compared!"
translations.idiomatic: Su said, "The Qian'er are Qiang; the Houmochen are barbarians—how can they be compared!"

sentences.zh: 素意以虜優羌劣。

translations.literal: Su's meaning was that barbarians were superior and Qiang inferior.
translations.idiomatic: Su meant that barbarians ranked above the Qiang.

sentences.zh: 琮曰：「以羌異虜，未之前聞。」

translations.literal: Cong said, "That Qiang differ from barbarians is something never heard of before."
translations.idiomatic: Cong said, "That the Qiang differ from barbarians is something I have never heard before."

sentences.zh: 素慚而止。

translations.literal: Su, ashamed, stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Su, ashamed, said no more.

sentences.zh: 琮雖羈旅，見北間豪貴，無所降下。

translations.literal: Though Cong was a guest in exile, when he met the great and noble of the north he bowed to none.
translations.idiomatic: Though Cong lived as an exile in the north, he bowed to none of its great nobles.

sentences.zh: 嘗與賀若弼深相友善，弼既被誅，複有童謠曰：「蕭蕭亦複起。」

translations.literal: He had once been deeply friendly with He Ruo Bi; after Bi was executed, there was again a children's song saying, "Xiao, xiao—again they rise."
translations.idiomatic: He had been close friends with He Ruobi. After Ruobi was executed, a children's song ran, "Xiao, xiao—they rise again."

sentences.zh: 帝由是忌之，遂廢於家，未幾而卒。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore grew suspicious of him, had him confined at home, and before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew suspicious and confined him at home. He died not long afterward.

sentences.zh: 贈左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was posthumously conferred as Grand Master of the Left Light.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Master of the Left Light.

sentences.zh: 子鉉，襄城通守。

translations.literal: His son Xian was Defender of Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xian was defender of Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 複以琮弟子钜為梁公。

translations.literal: Cong's nephew Ju was again made Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Cong's nephew Ju was then made Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 钜小名藏，煬帝甚昵之，以為千牛，與宇文皛出入宮掖，伺察內外。

translations.literal: Ju, whose childhood name was Zang, was greatly favored by Emperor Yang; he was made an attendant of the Thousand-Ox Guard and, together with Yuwen Xiao, went in and out of the palace women's quarters, observing within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Ju, childhood name Zang, was greatly favored by Emperor Yang. He was made an attendant of the Thousand-Ox Guard and, with Yuwen Xiao, went in and out of the inner palace, watching affairs within and without.

sentences.zh: 帝每有遊宴，钜未嘗不從焉，遂于宮中多行淫穢。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor held excursions and banquets, Ju never failed to follow; he thereupon committed many lewd and filthy acts within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor held excursions and banquets, Ju was always present, and he committed many lewd acts within the palace.

sentences.zh: 江都之變，為宇文化及所殺。

translations.literal: At the Jiangdu upheaval he was killed by Yuwen Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: At the Jiangdu upheaval he was killed by Yuwen Huaji.

sentences.zh: 瓛字欽文，少聰敏，解屬文。

translations.literal: Huan, styled Qinwen, was from youth clever and keen and skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Huan, styled Qinwen, was clever from youth and skilled in literary composition.

sentences.zh: 在梁為荊州刺史，頗有能名。

translations.literal: In Liang he was Governor of Jing province and had a considerable reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang he was governor of Jing province and had a considerable reputation for ability.

sentences.zh: 崔弘度以兵至鄀州，瓛懼，與其叔父岩奔于陳。

translations.literal: When Cui Hongdu came with troops to Ruo prefecture, Huan was afraid; together with his uncle Yan he fled to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Hongdu brought troops to Ruo prefecture, Huan fled to Chen with his uncle Yan.

sentences.zh: 陳主以為侍中、安東將軍、吳州刺史，甚得物情，三吳父老皆曰：「瓛吾君子也。」

translations.literal: The Lord of Chen made him Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the East, and Governor of Wu prefecture; he won the hearts of men greatly, and the elders of the Three Wu all said, "Huan is our gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: The Chen ruler made him attendant-in-ordinary, General Who Pacifies the East, and governor of Wu prefecture. He won great favor, and the elders of the Three Wu said, "Huan is our true gentleman."

sentences.zh: 及陳亡，吳人推瓛為主。

translations.literal: When Chen perished, the people of Wu urged Huan as their leader.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell, the people of Wu urged Huan to lead them.

sentences.zh: 吳人見梁武、簡文及詧、巋等兄弟並第三而踐尊位，瓛自以巋之第三子也，深自矜負。

translations.literal: The people of Wu saw that Emperor Wu of Liang, Emperor Jianwen, and the brothers Cha and Kui had all been third sons and yet ascended the honored throne; Huan, considering himself Kui's third son, deeply prided himself on this.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wu noted that Emperor Wu of Liang, Emperor Jianwen, and the brothers Cha and Kui had all been third sons yet reached the throne. Huan, as Kui's third son, took great pride in this.

sentences.zh: 有謝異者，頗知廢興，梁、陳之際，言無不驗，江南人甚敬信之。

translations.literal: There was one Xie Yi who was well versed in rise and fall; in the transition between Liang and Chen, nothing he said failed to come true, and the people of Jiangnan greatly revered and trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Xie Yi was skilled at reading the rise and fall of states. In the transition between Liang and Chen, nothing he said failed to come true, and the people of Jiangnan greatly revered him.

sentences.zh: 及陳主被擒，異奔於瓛，由是益為眾所歸。

translations.literal: When the Lord of Chen was captured, Yi fled to Huan; thereby Huan came to be still more followed by the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chen ruler was captured, Yi fled to Huan, and Huan gained still more support.

sentences.zh: 褒國公宇文述以兵討之，瓛遣王哀守吳州，自將拒述。

translations.literal: Duke of Baoguo Yuwen Shu came with troops to suppress him; Huan sent Wang Ai to hold Wu prefecture and personally led the army to resist Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Baoguo Yuwen Shu came with troops to suppress him. Huan sent Wang Ai to hold Wu prefecture and personally led the army against Shu.

sentences.zh: 述遣兵別道襲吳州，哀懼，衣道士服，棄城而遁。

translations.literal: Shu sent troops by a separate route to strike Wu prefecture; Ai was afraid, put on a Daoist priest's robe, abandoned the city, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Shu sent troops by another route to strike Wu prefecture. Ai, terrified, dressed as a Daoist priest, abandoned the city, and fled.

sentences.zh: 瓛眾聞之，悉無鬥志，與述一戰而敗。

translations.literal: When Huan's host heard of it, they all lost fighting spirit; after one battle with Shu they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan's troops heard of this, they lost all fighting spirit. After one battle with Shu they were defeated.

sentences.zh: 瓛將左右數人逃於太湖，匿於民家，為人所執，送於述所，斬之長安，時年二十一。

translations.literal: Huan took a few attendants and fled to Lake Tai, hiding in a commoner's house; he was seized by someone, sent to Shu's camp, and beheaded in Chang'an at the age of twenty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Huan fled to Lake Tai with a few attendants and hid in a commoner's house. He was seized, sent to Shu, and beheaded in Chang'an at the age of twenty-one.

sentences.zh: 弟璟，為朝請大夫、尚衣奉禦。

translations.literal: His younger brother Jing was a Grand Master for Imperial Audience and Attendant for Imperial Vestments.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Jing was a grand master for imperial audience and attendant for imperial vestments.

sentences.zh: 瑒，曆衛尉卿、秘書監、陶丘侯。

translations.literal: Yang successively held the offices of Commandant of the Guards for the Palace, Director of the Palace Library, and Marquis of Taoqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang served as commandant of the guards for the palace, director of the palace library, and Marquis of Taoqiu.

sentences.zh: 瑀，曆內史侍郎、河池太守。

translations.literal: Yu successively held the offices of Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat and Governor of Hechi.
translations.idiomatic: Yu served as vice director of the palace secretariat and governor of Hechi.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：三五哲王，防深慮遠，舅甥之國，罕執鈞衡，母后之家，無聞傾敗。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The sage kings of the Three Five eras guarded deeply and thought far; in states of maternal uncles and nephews, few held the balance of power; in households of empresses' kin, none were heard to topple and fail.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: The sage kings of antiquity guarded against danger and thought far ahead. Among states ruled by maternal uncles and nephews, few held real power; among empresses' kin, none were heard to fall into ruin.

sentences.zh: 爰及漢、晉，顛覆繼軌，皆由乎進不以禮，故其斃亦速。

translations.literal: Down to Han and Jin, overturn followed in succession—all because advancement did not follow ritual, and therefore their destruction was also swift.
translations.idiomatic: Down through Han and Jin, ruin came in succession—all because promotion did not follow proper ritual, and so their fall came quickly as well.

sentences.zh: 若使獨孤權侔呂、霍，必敗于仁壽之前，蕭氏勢均梁、竇，豈全于大業之後！

translations.literal: Had the Dugu clan's power matched that of Lü and Huo, they would surely have been defeated before Renshou; had the Xiao clan's strength equaled that of Liang and Dou, how could they have been preserved whole after the Daye era!
translations.idiomatic: Had the Dugu held power equal to the Lü and Huo clans, they would surely have fallen before the Renshou period; had the Xiao matched the Liang and Dou in strength, how could they have survived intact after the Daye era!

sentences.zh: 今或不隕舊基，或更隆先構，豈非處之以道，不預權寵之所致乎！

translations.literal: That some today did not fall from their old foundations, or even raised their ancestors' structures higher—was this not caused by being treated according to the Way and not being admitted to power and favor!
translations.idiomatic: That some did not fall from their old foundations, or even raised their ancestors' standing higher—was this not because they were treated with proper restraint and kept from power and favor!
